weight-quantization.name: weight quantization
weight-quantization.definition: Representing model weights on a lower-precision numerical grid.
weight-quantization.explanation: Quantization maps each floating-point weight to an integer code plus metadata such as a scale and possibly a zero point. Reconstruction is approximate because many real values share one code. Finer groups or per-channel scales can reduce quantization error at the cost of metadata and more complex kernels. Storage reduction, task quality, and runtime are separate outcomes and must be measured separately.

weight-only-quantization.name: weight-only quantization
weight-only-quantization.definition: Quantizing weights while activations or accumulation remain floating point.
weight-only-quantization.explanation: A weight-only kernel stores compact integer weight codes but accepts floating-point activations. It may dequantize weights during the dot product and accumulate in floating point. This can reduce persistent model storage and weight traffic without requiring activation calibration. It is distinct from integer-only inference, which quantizes activations too and usually uses wider integer accumulators plus output rescaling after each operation.

dequantization.name: dequantization
dequantization.definition: Reconstructing an approximate real value from a quantized code.
dequantization.explanation: For symmetric quantization, dequantization multiplies signed code q by positive scale s to obtain the approximation sq. It can happen before computation or inside a fused matrix kernel. Materializing a full floating-point matrix is simple but forfeits bandwidth savings during repeated inference. On-the-fly conversion preserves compact storage but adds instructions and needs a layout suited to the target hardware and vector operations.
